judgeRationales.scenarioName: Advise on xUnit v2 to v3 without framework conversion
judgeRationales.rationale: A supplies the requested xUnit v3 migration while preserving the project's VSTest/Visual Studio runner route. B's central recommendation replaces that route with an MSBuild/Microsoft Testing Platform runner strategy, conflicting with the requested runner-compatibility framing and omitting key VSTest preservation guidance.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert IClassFixture to ClassInitialize
judgeRationales.rationale: Both outputs indicate a compiling, passing package/assertion migration, but B performs the specified MSTest class-fixture lifecycle conversion. A's simplified instance fixture omits the required static initialization, cleanup, and static usage, materially changing fixture lifetime and missing most rubric requirements.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert ITestOutputHelper to TestContext
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert MemberData and TheoryData to DynamicData
judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs produce a verified, working MSTest conversion, but B better preserves the original IEnumerable<object[]> source shape and also reports cleaning its analyzer warning. The main functional result is otherwise comparable.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert Skip, Trait, and Timeout
judgeRationales.rationale: Both appear to have completed a correct conversion satisfying every rubric item. B's final report is more specific about the source packages, exact target packages, concrete semantic mappings, and discovery totals. A has the marginally stronger evidence that its final written state was tested after edits, but B's result remains more clearly documented overall.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert xUnit v3 TestContext.Current.CancellationToken
judgeRationales.rationale: B performs the semantically correct MSTest conversion and verifies it passes. Although A also compiles and passes, it replaces the actual test-context cancellation contract with a fresh, uncancelled CTS token, directly failing every stated migration requirement.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Handle ICollectionFixture explicitly (do not silently widen scope)
judgeRationales.rationale: Both appear to produce passing MSTest conversions with the required class serialization, but B gives materially clearer evidence that the database fixture remains a single shared Lazy-backed fixture. Neither adequately documents the scope-mapping decision, so the advantage is modest.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Identify conflicting and shared inherited owners before editing
judgeRationales.rationale: B provides the key project-specific migration blocker: one inherited test is shared across two derived classes with divergent class owners and assembly metadata, making a lossless automatic method-level Owner conversion impossible. A gives only a generic metadata-conflict discussion and misses this decisive detail.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Map exception assertions correctly (xUnit Throws -> MSTest ThrowsExactly)
judgeRationales.rationale: B performs the canonical MSTest migration and explicitly preserves exact, derived-type, and async exception semantics. A's suite passes, but it uses older strict APIs and a concrete-type workaround instead of the proper general ThrowsAny-to-Throws conversion.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate basic xUnit v2 project to MSTest v4 preserving VSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate basic xUnit v3 project to MSTest v4 preserving VSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Both migrations appear functionally successful and validated under VSTest. B more precisely follows the requested Theory/InlineData mapping and additionally cleaned an MSTest analyzer warning; the gap is modest because A also passes all tests and meets the core conversion requirements.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve AwesomeAssertions package and every import form
judgeRationales.rationale: The two responses demonstrate equivalent successful migrations and equivalent validation. B is marginally more explicit about the exact MSTest package versions and skipped count, but this does not establish a material quality advantage over A.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve effective assembly and class owners on methods
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve type and sequence assertion semantics
judgeRationales.rationale: Both conversions build and pass tests while retaining the key framework and sequence behavior. B is preferable because it uses the appropriate MSTest exact-type API and, crucially, preserves typed assertion return values rather than reducing the exact-type assertion to a boolean expression.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve xUnit parallelization default with [assembly: Parallelize]
judgeRationales.rationale: Both completed a validated xUnit-to-MSTest conversion, preserved class-level parallelization with the exact requested attribute, and reported two passing tests. Their minor differences in package choice and detail do not establish a meaningful quality advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recognize project already on MSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stop when target framework is unsupported by MSTest v4
judgeRationales.rationale: B performs a validated conversion using the latest MSTest v4 release and correctly explains the framework compatibility issue. Its central deficiency is silently retargeting the project, which violates the confirmation requirement. A also silently retargets, while additionally using an older v3 MSTest package and omitting the key compatibility explanation.

verdictEvidence.reason: Net win +80.0% (4W/1T/0L over 5 preference-eligible stimulus vote(s), sign test p=0.063), mean preference +56.7% across 6 paired run(s), 1 dormancy stimulus/stimuli excluded from preference — not credible — 1 of 5 preference-eligible stimulus vote(s) tied, leaving only 4 discordant preference vote(s). The sign test conditions on non-tie stimulus votes and cannot reach 0.05 below 5, so no record could have passed here — this is not a measured null. Either the agent is inert on these scenarios (make them discriminate) or the eval needs more distinct stimuli to clear the ties — native evaluator reported an objective task-completion regression

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: baseline, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detect MSTest v2 on VSTest and recommend migration path
judgeRationales.rationale: B fully answers the requested migration assessment: it accurately identifies the framework/version, determines the current platform, and supplies the staged v2→v3→v4 path plus the optional MTP migration. A correctly detects MSTest 2.2.10 but provides an incomplete and somewhat outdated migration framing.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detect xUnit v2 and route to xUnit v3 migration
judgeRationales.rationale: B provides a concrete completed migration with verified package versions, explains runner behavior, checks the test source for common v3 incompatibilities, and honestly notes that test execution could not be verified. A is broadly informative but less actionable and includes questionable runner-removal guidance.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Execute targeted MSTest v2 to v3 migration

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Correctly identify MSTest v1 vs v2 and recommend different migration paths
judgeRationales.rationale: Both give the key distinction between the two starting points correctly, but B is more aligned with the intended v1/v2-to-v3 migration: it explicitly names v3 as the target and clearly states that the paths converge after the differing initial step.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Execute and verify MSTest v2 to v3 migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Fix Assert.AreEqual object overload errors after v3 upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: Both produce the same correct source changes and passing tests. B is marginally stronger because it confirms the initial three errors, performs an explicit post-fix build as well as the test run, and communicates the verification more precisely.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Fix DataRow type mismatch errors after v3 upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: Both produce the correct source fix and verified passing result. B is modestly better because its technical explanation correctly characterizes the conversion and accurately contextualizes the 17-parameter DataRow support.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Handle dropped target framework during v3 migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Both give the essential framework answer accurately. B is more migration-complete and current: it recommends a current LTS target, notes netcoreapp3.1 EOL, and provides useful package and breaking-change guidance. A did apply an edit, but its choice of net6.0 and MSTest 3.0.0 is less current for a new migration.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate MSTest v1 project with assembly reference
judgeRationales.rationale: Both provide the core project-file migration accurately, and A usefully validates a concrete edit. However, B is materially more reliable migration guidance because it covers the key Assert.AreEqual breaking change (and other relevant v3 compatibility checks), while A makes an overbroad and incorrect claim that no code changes are needed.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate MSTest v2 NuGet project to v3
judgeRationales.rationale: B is substantially more complete against the migration rubric, ties its findings to the visible project, and distinguishes applicable changes from watch items. Although its metapackage wording is more prescriptive than necessary, it is preferable overall; A also contains a questionable timeout assertion and omits several important v3 migration risks.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate complex MSTest v2 project with testsettings, DataRow issues, and dropped TFM
judgeRationales.rationale: The responses produce substantively identical, complete migrations and verification. Response B is a little more concise while Response A includes a little more context, but neither has a meaningful quality advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate from .testsettings to .runsettings
judgeRationales.rationale: B performs the required replacement with the correct MSTest v3 deployment configuration and per-test timeout. A's key deployment conversion is incorrect even though its XML is accepted syntactically, so it does not reliably preserve the requested behavior.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate to MSTest.Sdk project style
judgeRationales.rationale: Both answers deliver the essential conversion and package cleanup, but B is more complete and reliable: it explicitly addresses the default runner behavior, gives a compatibility-preserving project file, and validates the migrated project and necessary v3 source fixes.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stop when the project already uses MSTest v3
judgeRationales.rationale: Both final results are correct and appropriately leave the already-v3 project untouched. B is modestly stronger because its final report supplies more relevant verification for the no-op conclusion without proposing unnecessary upgrades.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Address TreatDiscoveryWarningsAsErrors and behavioral changes
judgeRationales.rationale: B correctly addresses both independent issues, especially the central discovery-warning default and its concrete configuration workaround. A is good on TestContext lifetime but misleadingly dismisses the separate v4 discovery behavior and therefore fails a major part of the task.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Correctly identify MSTest v3 project and recommend v4 migration
judgeRationales.rationale: A is more reliable for this project: it gives the actual current package version, applies the directly relevant fixes, and verifies tests pass. B is broader on behavioral changes, but its outdated 'latest' version claim is a meaningful defect for a user explicitly asking to upgrade to the latest.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Fix Assert.IsInstanceOfType out parameter removal
judgeRationales.rationale: The substantive migration guidance is equally correct, but B gives slightly more concrete coverage of all three affected assertions and additionally reports that the migrated tests passed, not merely that the project built.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Fix TestMethodAttribute CallerInfo constructor breaking change
judgeRationales.rationale: Both explain the core API change and property-based display name fix, but B includes the important caller-info propagation required for a faithful v4 subclass migration. Neither explicitly demonstrates the direct [TestMethod(DisplayName = ...)] syntax.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Fix TestMethodAttribute and TestMethod display name constructor
judgeRationales.rationale: The core migration advice is equivalently correct in both responses, and B usefully covers derived attributes. However, A goes further by applying the requested edits to all three tests and confirming the upgraded project builds, making it the better completion of this task.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Fix multiple v4 breaking changes: Assert, ClassCleanup, TestContext, Timeout
judgeRationales.rationale: Both successfully fix the observed assertion and cleanup API breaks, repair the unrelated constant-division compile error, and report passing tests. B is better because it applies the expected TestTimeout.Infinite migration to int.MaxValue; A's timeout guidance is materially incorrect relative to the migration requirement.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Fix sealed custom TestMethodAttribute with Timeout changes
judgeRationales.rationale: B addresses every material source migration issue, builds cleanly apart from unrelated assertion warnings, and verifies tests pass. A fixes the immediate compile errors but omits the caller-info constructor propagation and incorrectly dismisses the resulting analyzer warning as pre-existing/unrelated.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Full MSTest v3 to v4 migration with multiple breaking changes
judgeRationales.rationale: B delivers a concise, technically targeted migration plan covering every rubric item and several relevant compatibility/verification considerations. A's final answer contains no plan at all, regardless of information visible in its untrusted timeline.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Handle MSTest.Sdk and MTP changes in v4
judgeRationales.rationale: B accurately addresses all requested aspects, especially the actual MSTest.Sdk v4 transitive-reference breaking change and explicit repair. A centers an incorrect or at least materially misleading cause, omits the explicit Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk fix, and overclaims successful validation despite an unresolved testhost failure.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Handle net6.0 target framework dropped in MSTest v4
judgeRationales.rationale: Both give the core compatibility answer correctly. B is marginally more useful through an immediately applicable csproj change and a broader, well-organized set of source and behavioral migration considerations; A is also accurate and strong.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate MSTest.Sdk v3 project using ManagedType and TestTimeout
judgeRationales.rationale: B supplies the correct migration for all three reported compiler failures and additionally covers the relevant Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk/MTP change. A is correct on timeout and ContainsKey, but its central ManagedType replacement is materially wrong.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate custom TestMethodAttribute from Execute to ExecuteAsync
judgeRationales.rationale: A is clearer as a standalone code migration example, but B covers the deadlock rationale required by the rubric and additionally calls out caller-info constructor propagation, a relevant v4 custom-attribute compatibility detail. The advantage is limited because B's final response omits the actual edited code.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Replace ExpectedExceptionAttribute with Assert.ThrowsExactly
judgeRationales.rationale: Both answers are technically correct and practical, with comparable examples and useful async/type-matching guidance. B is overall better because it additionally supplies the requested relevant MSTEST0006 migration context.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Understand behavioral changes after MSTest v4 upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: Both directly and correctly answer the two reported v4 changes and meet every listed rubric item. A is slightly stronger overall because it supplies a source link, more precise explanatory context, and a substantially broader, useful set of relevant v4 migration issues. B is concise and includes a valuable MTP/vstest compatibility warning, but its discovery-warning consequence is less clearly stated.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Verified MSTest v3 to v4 package update with build and test
judgeRationales.rationale: Both complete the requested migration and verification successfully. A is marginally more technically precise in its explanation of the TestTimeout breaking change.

judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses correctly migrate the theory, preserve the complete data cross-product and inconclusive behavior, and verify the required test outcome. judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert cooperative cancellation attribute
judgeRationales.rationale: Both migrations satisfy every substantive requirement. B is marginally stronger in its final reporting: it identifies the newer MSTest 4.4.0 version, explicitly confirms the VSTest/global.json preservation, and gives the complete test totals. This is a presentation/current-package advantage rather than a material correctness gap.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate basic NUnit project while preserving VSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Both migrations meet the requested conversion and test successfully. B is slightly stronger for using a newer unified MSTest v4 package and explicitly fixing the compatible Test.Sdk version after detecting the downgrade. Its unnecessary serial-execution assertion is questionable, so the advantage is modest.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve NUnit pairwise case set
judgeRationales.rationale: Both appear to produce a correct, tested migration. B's final report is more precise and complete about the individual NUnit-to-MSTest mappings, package/version choice, runner preservation, and verification, although its temporary cleanup-attribute build error was corrected and does not impair the final result.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve NUnit single-instance fixture state
judgeRationales.rationale: Both migrations appear correct, use MSTest v4, preserve the shared state, and pass all tests. B is slightly better because its final report precisely calls out the critical fixture-instance lifecycle mismatch and verifies the migrated test count against the baseline.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve STA across async continuations
judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs reach the same correct MSTest v4 conversion, preserve async STA synchronization semantics, remove NUnit-specific test attributes, and verify the project builds successfully.

judgeRationales.rationale: Both migrations are substantively correct and pass the tests. A has marginally stronger end-to-end evidence for the required per-row category preservation by running and reporting the category-filtered test run.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Configure dotnet test MTP mode on .NET 10 SDK
judgeRationales.rationale: B correctly and concretely covers all requested migration points, including the essential global.json runner selection and direct MTP argument syntax. A gives only a terse, incomplete answer and misleadingly suggests EnableMSTestRunner alone is sufficient.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Full VSTest to MTP migration plan for MSTest solution
judgeRationales.rationale: B is materially more reliable for the stated .NET 8 migration: it correctly handles argument forwarding, supplies the important zero-tests exit-code caveat, and identifies a tested compatible TRX extension version. A is broader on coverage publishing and transition risks, but its core .NET 8 pipeline invocation is wrong and its adapter/removal guidance is internally inconsistent, which are serious migration-plan defects.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Handle exit code 8 when migrating from VSTest to MTP
judgeRationales.rationale: B satisfies every requested rubric item, notably including the environment-variable alternative, and gives strong scoping guidance. A's command invocation is more reliably formed, but its omission of the requested environment-variable route leaves B modestly more complete overall.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate MSTest project from VSTest to Microsoft.Testing.Platform
judgeRationales.rationale: B satisfies every requested migration detail, particularly explicit executable output, native TRX setup, and the .NET 8 argument separator. A has materially incorrect or misleading CI guidance and omits OutputType=Exe, so its proposed migration is not reliably correct.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate MSTest.Sdk project that explicitly uses VSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Both get the core project-file change right, but B provides the important SDK-version-dependent dotnet test integration and accurately explains the generated runner settings. A's claim that no other changes are required and that dotnet test still works by default is materially incomplete/misleading for the requested migration. [Magnitude reduced to "slightly-better": the position-swapped pass judged this "slightly-better", so the more confident "much-better" was downgraded.]

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate NUnit project from VSTest to Microsoft.Testing.Platform
judgeRationales.rationale: B supplies the required early-evaluated NUnit runner and executable settings, appropriate dotnet-test native-MTP opt-in, a compatible adapter version, and validates the migration. A misses core required settings and contains misleading claims about the runner, bridge support, and direct execution.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate xUnit.net VSTest filter syntax to MTP
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly provides the correct native xUnit v3 MTP filter flags, wildcard semantics, AND behavior, and a query-form alternative. A contains materially misleading flag names and an incorrect/inapplicable filter option, despite correctly conveying the high-level migration idea.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate xUnit.net v2 project from VSTest to Microsoft.Testing.Platform
judgeRationales.rationale: B gives a working, verified migration using an available pinned adapter version and correct native .NET 10 integration. A is broader and has a better cleanup note, but its recommendation of unavailable YTest.MTP.XUnit2 0.4.0 is a meaningful actionable defect.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Set OutputType=Exe only for test projects in Directory.Build.props
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Translate dotnet test VSTest arguments to MTP equivalents
judgeRationales.rationale: A gives one coherent command that preserves every requested behavior, including crash-dump collection. B ultimately supplies a correct alternate, but presents an incomplete primary command and an erroneous/ambiguous caveat about the crash-dump mapping.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update Azure DevOps pipeline from VSTest task to MTP
judgeRationales.rationale: A provides a genuinely working MTP migration, including verified TRX and Cobertura generation and coverage publication. B has a useful YAML excerpt and separator explanation, but its Directory.Build.props condition does not match TestProject, leaving the runner properties unapplied; its own test output confirms legacy VSTest execution, so it fails the core migration.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Advise on xUnit v2 to v3 without framework conversion
judgeRationales.rationale: Although A is more project-specific, its core runner recommendation wrongly treats native MTP as the only practical v3 route and removes the requested VSTest compatibility. B directly explains both supported routes and how to retain VSTest, making it the more useful answer despite several generic and questionable technical details.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert IClassFixture to ClassInitialize
judgeRationales.rationale: Both produce a valid, verified MSTest conversion that satisfies every listed fixture-migration requirement. B provides more package/version and runner rationale, while A uses the conventional explicit framework/adapter references; neither yields a material final-result advantage for this project.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert ITestOutputHelper to TestContext
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert MemberData and TheoryData to DynamicData
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert Skip, Trait, and Timeout
judgeRationales.rationale: Both complete and verify a working migration, but B is substantively more correct because it preserves the Owner trait using MSTest's dedicated [Owner] attribute. A fails that explicit conversion requirement.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert xUnit v3 TestContext.Current.CancellationToken
judgeRationales.rationale: Although both runs build and pass the single test and correctly migrate the core attributes/packages, B makes the required direct MSTest cancellation-token migration. A's use of CancellationTokenSource violates two explicit requirements.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Handle ICollectionFixture explicitly (do not silently widen scope)
judgeRationales.rationale: B is preferable because it explicitly and robustly enforces non-parallel execution with [DoNotParallelize], the central behavioral requirement. A has a somewhat stronger fixture lifecycle implementation, but its reliance on a default runner setting leaves the serialization guarantee fragile and fails the explicit criterion.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Identify conflicting and shared inherited owners before editing
judgeRationales.rationale: A reaches the key conclusion: existing Owner metadata cannot be preserved automatically because xUnit traits are additive and can contain multiple values. B's central semantic error (treating trait layering as last-wins) causes it to miss required user decisions, so its otherwise useful mechanical migration notes do not rescue the assessment.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Map exception assertions correctly (xUnit Throws -> MSTest ThrowsExactly)
judgeRationales.rationale: B correctly performs all three specified exception assertion mappings with MSTest v4 and verifies the migrated suite. A passes the current tests but fails the key exception-semantics requirements, especially the ThrowsAny conversion.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate basic xUnit v2 project to MSTest v4 preserving VSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Both complete the code-level migration and preserve VSTest, but B uniquely fulfills the central package-management requirement to use the MSTest metapackage and refresh the stale Test SDK. A's older separate framework/adapter package approach is functional but does not meet that requested package configuration. [Magnitude reduced to "slightly-better": the position-swapped pass judged this "slightly-better", so the more confident "much-better" was downgraded.]

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate basic xUnit v3 project to MSTest v4 preserving VSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Both are correct, complete conversions that pass the expected three tests. B is marginally stronger in documenting and checking preservation of the VSTest runner and cleaning up the former xUnit-v3 executable output setting, while A's explicit framework/adapter package approach is also fully valid.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve AwesomeAssertions package and every import form
judgeRationales.rationale: Both produce a valid MSTest v4/net8.0/VSTest migration that preserves the requested assertion setup and passes both tests. B's baseline verification and explicit count are marginally nicer reporting, but its extra parallelization file is unnecessary; neither yields a meaningful final-result advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve effective assembly and class owners on methods
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve type and sequence assertion semantics
judgeRationales.rationale: Both migrations are correct and verified, but B is cleaner and more semantically direct: it uses the newer dedicated MSTest exact-type and sequence assertion APIs and preserves typed assertion-result usage without auxiliary casts.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve xUnit parallelization default with [assembly: Parallelize]
judgeRationales.rationale: Both completed the same correct, verified migration: xUnit dependencies and constructs were replaced with MSTest equivalents, class-level parallelization was configured correctly, and two tests passed. Their final reports are comparably clear; neither satisfies the one missing explicit-default-serial explanation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recognize project already on MSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Both reach the correct no-change conclusion and avoid destructive edits, but B provides the requested build/test verification. Its erroneous reference to MSTest v4 despite package version 3.8.0 prevents a larger advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stop when target framework is unsupported by MSTest v4
judgeRationales.rationale: B produces a correct, build-verified net7-compatible MSTest migration and, crucially, explains why MSTest v4 cannot satisfy the existing TFM. Its main shortcoming is proceeding with the v3 fallback without requesting confirmation, but A has the same confirmation deficiency plus lacks the compatibility analysis and uses a substantially older MSTest version.

A verifies only compilation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert async void test methods to async Task
judgeRationales.rationale: Both perform the essential source migration and report three passing tests, but B better handles the project's VSTest configuration via IsTestingPlatformApplication=false and verifies the intended `dotnet test` workflow with a clean build. A leaves `dotnet test` failing and substitutes direct executable execution, while also giving a less precise async-void explanation.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detect incompatible target framework and stop migration
judgeRationales.rationale: B follows the expected compatibility-gate behavior exactly: it recognizes the unsupported framework, makes no migration changes, and instructs the user to upgrade first. Although A produces a plausibly working migrated project, it ignores the task's required stop condition and fails two of three rubric criteria.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate Xunit.SkippableFact to xUnit.net v3 built-in skip APIs
judgeRationales.rationale: Both produce a working v3 migration and verify the default skipped behavior. B adheres more exactly to every specified API conversion and additionally verifies an enabled feature branch; A's declarative alternative is reasonable but is less aligned with the stated Skip.IfNot-to-Assert.SkipUnless requirement.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate basic xUnit.net v2 project to v3
judgeRationales.rationale: Both perform the core package migration and pass all tests, but B supplies the key VSTest compatibility setting required by the rubric and avoids changing the test runner mode. A's missing property and switch to Microsoft.Testing.Platform make its resulting project configuration less correct for the original setup.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate project with YTest.MTP.XUnit2 to xUnit.net v3 preserving MTP
judgeRationales.rationale: The resulting migrations are substantively identical, satisfy every rubric item, and are validated by a successful one-test MTP run. Response B's statement that 4.0.1 is the latest stable is somewhat imprecise given the visible availability of 4.0.2, but it does not affect the correct restored final project and is not enough to distinguish the final result.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate xUnit v2 packages managed via Central Package Management
judgeRationales.rationale: Both produce tested, functioning migrations and correctly use central package management. B is better because it satisfies the explicit executable-output requirement and makes a conventional, contained v3 migration that preserves the existing VSTest configuration; A omits OutputType and instead changes the repository-wide test-runner setting.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recognize project already on xUnit.net v3 — no migration needed
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update BeforeAfterTestAttribute overrides with IXunitTest parameter
judgeRationales.rationale: Both appear to deliver a working v3 migration and verify passing tests. B is slightly stronger because its final report precisely documents the required base-call changes and exact API migration, while preserving the existing VSTest setup rather than introducing a global runner change.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update Xunit.Combinatorial and Xunit.StaFact companion packages
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy the stated migration requirements, but B additionally adds EnableWindowsTargeting, verifies a clean zero-warning/zero-error build on the Linux host, and accurately distinguishes the remaining runtime test-launch limitation. A leaves the project failing to build in that environment and incorrectly treats the cross-targeting build issue as unavoidable.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Decline request to write new tests
judgeRationales.rationale: Response A provides slightly better test coverage by explicitly addressing overflow behavior, which is an important edge case for integer arithmetic that Response B doesn't mention. However, Response B was slightly more efficient in its exploration approach. Both responses successfully completed the task with all tests passing. The difference is marginal—this is a close call where Response A edges ahead primarily due to more comprehensive edge case coverage (overflow), but the practical difference between the two implementations is minimal.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detect MSTest v2 on VSTest and recommend migration path
judgeRationales.rationale: While Response B had 5 tool call errors (failed view attempts for non-existent files), the quality of its final output is significantly better. Response B correctly addresses all four rubric criteria: it identifies the MSTest version, explicitly calls out the VSTest platform (which A missed), recommends the v3 upgrade path specifically, and details both the MSTest progression (v2→v3→v4) and the VSTest→MTP alternative migration. Response A is cleaner operationally (fewer errors, fewer tools) but provides incomplete and less precise guidance, missing key distinctions about the test platform and version progression that are central to the task. The substance of Response B's answer is substantially more complete and accurate to what the user needs to know.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detect xUnit v2 and route to xUnit v3 migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Excellent execution that fully satisfied the task requirements and rubric criteria. The agent not only identified and recommended the xUnit v3 migration but actually implemented it completely with proper version resolution, applied all necessary configuration changes, and verified success by running the test suite (all 4 tests passed). The output was clear, comprehensive, and actionable. The agent demonstrated strong error recovery when the initial bash command was rejected, pivoting smoothly to alternative methods. The systematic approach (inspect → research → apply → verify) was methodical and efficient. Minor deduction would only apply if considering the one recorded error, but given the successful recovery and final positive outcome, this does not warrant score reduction from 5.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Execute targeted MSTest v2 to v3 migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B delivers a complete, verified, working migration while Response A's approach is incomplete and would likely fail in a fresh build. The critical differences: (1) Response B recognized and fixed the Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk compatibility requirement (v3 requires ≥17.13.0), (2) Response B identified and fixed the missing `System` import that would cause compilation failure, (3) Response B verified test success with actual passing tests, whereas Response A's test run with --no-restore doesn't validate a clean build, (4) Response B had no errors while Response A had 1 error. While both technically 'upgraded' the package version numbers, only Response B ensured the migration actually works end-to-end.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Execute targeted xUnit v2 to v3 migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Response A did not complete the core task requirement of making the project build. It acknowledged this failure explicitly. Response B not only completed the migration with necessary configuration changes but also verified success with actual test execution (4/4 passing). While both encountered environmental constraints, Response B overcame them effectively. The OutputType and IsTestingPlatformApplication properties Response B added are required by xUnit v3's architectural changes (moving from library to executable), not extraneous modifications. Response B delivered a fully functional, verified migration; Response A delivered an incomplete one.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Plan a staged MSTest v2 to v4 and MTP migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B is significantly superior because it correctly addresses the rubric's core requirement: explicitly including the v2→v3 intermediate migration step that Response A completely omits. This is not a minor detail—jumping directly from v2 to v4 is risky and prevents proper isolation of issues. Additionally, Response B provides far more actionable validation gates with specific error codes, API names, concrete commands to execute, and exact code changes required (e.g., Assert.ThrowsException→Assert.ThrowsExactly). Response B is structured for professional execution with measurable gates, while Response A is more narrative and generic. Both maintain the plan-only constraint, but Response B delivers substantially higher quality planning that would be far more reliable for actual implementation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Fix DataRow type mismatch errors after v3 upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses correctly diagnose and fix the MSTest v3 type-matching issue, converting 1L/2L to 1/2 and preserving the 17-parameter test. The technical outcomes are equivalent (all 3 tests pass). However, Response B provides a more explicit and detailed deliverable: it clearly articulates why the 17-parameter test was preserved (MSTest 3.8.0 support), provides precise test results (3 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped), and explains each decision more transparently. Response A's understanding is solid, but its final output is less detailed. The difference is modest—both accomplish the task well—but Response B's clearer communication about the reasoning and results gives it a slight edge.

Response A provides generic guidance without project analysis and critically omits the Assert.AreEqual breaking change, which could cause runtime failures after migration."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate MSTest v2 NuGet project to v3

It explicitly identifies the project version, offers clear upgrade paths, provides concrete examples (error codes, type literals), organizes information in a scannable table format with project-specific status, and critically warns that compilation success won't detect all breaking changes. Response A is accurate and covers the major issues but presents them less clearly and with less practical detail. Both responses address all rubric criteria, but Response B does so more thoroughly and usefully."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate basic xUnit v3 project to MSTest v4 preserving VSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B provides a more thorough, verifiable migration. It explicitly documents all attribute conversions, provides concrete grep verification that all xunit patterns are removed from the final codebase, upgrades Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk while maintaining VSTest compatibility, and includes clear final inspection of migrated files. Response A succeeds functionally (tests pass) but lacks detailed verification and has truncated output that obscures key conversion details, particularly around [InlineData] → [DataRow] conversion. Both complete the task successfully, but B demonstrates superior methodology and verification practices."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve AwesomeAssertions package and every import form
judgeRationales.rationale: Response A is slightly better overall because it ran explicit contract verification against the provided evaluation scripts (.eval/assertion_contract.py and .eval/runner_contract.py), confirming that AwesomeAssertions imports and the package were preserved. This is objective evidence of meeting the rubric criteria, whereas Response B only claims preservation without verification. Additionally, Response A preserved the original SDK version, demonstrating alignment with the 'preserving' requirement. Both responses successfully migrated the tests and achieved 2/2 passing, but Response A provides stronger evidence of correctness through its explicit contract verification."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve effective assembly and class owners on methods
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve type and sequence assertion semantics
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses successfully migrate the project and run all tests passing. However, Response B excels in documentation and transparency: it explicitly lists the specific MSTest methods used to preserve exact-type checks, assignable-type checks, and element-by-element sequence comparison. Response B also demonstrates more methodical problem-solving by proactively identifying and addressing the SDK version constraint before encountering test failures, whereas Response A recovered from a compilation failure. While both achieve the end goal, Response B's superior clarity on semantic preservation, more efficient execution path, and explicit reasoning about design decisions make it the stronger response overall.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve xUnit parallelization default with [assembly: Parallelize]
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B is slightly better because it explicitly and clearly shows the complete assembly-level parallelization directive `[assembly: Parallelize(Workers = 0, Scope = ExecutionScope.ClassLevel)]` in the final output summary. Response A claims to have enabled class-level parallelization but doesn't make the Workers = 0 parameter visible in its output summary, making it less clear that the correct and complete directive was added. Both achieve the functional goal of converting to MSTest and running tests successfully, but Response B provides better verification of the exact configuration required by the rubric."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recognize project already on MSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses correctly handle the core task: recognizing that MSTest is already in use and not performing any migration. However, Response B is more thorough in its verification, explicitly confirming no files were changed, providing more detailed test output metrics, and more directly communicating that migration is not needed. Response B also activated the migration skill and confirmed via inspection that no work was required, demonstrating more comprehensive verification. The differences are incremental but consistent across all rubric criteria, making Response B slightly stronger in quality of communication and verification rigor."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stop when target framework is unsupported by MSTest v4
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B correctly identified the critical incompatibility and followed proper procedure by stopping and requesting user approval before making any changes. Response A violated the core requirement by silently retargeting the framework from net7.0 to net8.0 without user consent. The rubric explicitly tests whether the agent respects breaking changes and seeks approval—Response B passes all three criteria decisively, while Response A fails on all counts by making unauthorized, breaking changes to the project configuration."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Consolidate xunit.extensibility packages and remove xunit.abstractions
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B correctly performs the xUnit v3 migration by using the proper v3 packages: xunit.v3.extensibility.core (consolidating the two v2 extensibility packages) and xunit.v3.core.mtp-off (ensuring VSTest compatibility). Response A fundamentally misapproaches the migration by replacing xunit.v3.extensibility.core with xunit.v3 alone, which is incorrect for a project requiring extensibility support (evidenced by CustomDiscoverer.cs). While both claim similar cleanup of abstractions, Response B's package choices align with xUnit v3's proper architecture, whereas Response A's approach of using the main framework package instead of the extensibility package is architecturally incorrect for this use case." [Magnitude reduced to "slightly-better": the position-swapped pass judged this "slightly-better", so the more confident "much-better" was downgraded.]

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert async void test methods to async Task
judgeRationales.rationale: While both responses successfully complete the core migration task—converting async void to async Task and updating packages to xUnit v3 with passing tests—Response B delivers a more modern and complete migration. It uses the latest xUnit v3 4.0.1 release (vs. 3.2.2), implements Testing Platform-appropriate configuration (OutputType=Exe, IsTestingPlatformApplication=false), and applies xUnit v3 best practices (CancellationToken handling for analyzer compliance). Response B's skill-based approach also demonstrates more structured domain knowledge. Neither response fully addresses the requirement to explain why async void is incompatible with v3, so both fall short on criterion 3. Overall, Response B represents a higher-quality, more forward-compatible migration that aligns with current xUnit v3 practices."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert string-based attribute constructors to typeof syntax
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B is slightly better because it provides clear, verifiable evidence that all migration steps were completed, particularly the critical CollectionBehavior conversion that Response A claims but doesn't demonstrate. Response B includes explicit file excerpts showing the converted attributes, uses a structured migration skill, and performs verification that no v2 patterns remain. While neither response excels at explaining the underlying API change (rubric criterion 3), Response B's superior documentation of completeness and verification makes it more reliable for this migration task."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detect incompatible target framework and stop migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B correctly follows all three rubric criteria, while Response A violates the critical criteria of stopping the migration and advising the user. Although Response A's automatic framework upgrade resulted in a working build, it disregarded explicit instructions to halt when a prerequisite constraint (minimum framework version) was discovered. Response B's approach—detecting the blocker, refusing to proceed, and clearly instructing the user to resolve it first—aligns with best practices for migration guidance and follows the stated requirements precisely."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate Xunit.SkippableFact to xUnit.net v3 built-in skip APIs
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B demonstrates a more complete and modern xUnit.v3 migration. It uses current package versions (4.0.1 vs 3.2.2), adds proper Testing Platform configuration (OutputType=Exe, IsTestingPlatformApplication=false), and provides better evidence of source code modifications through explicit script output. Both responses successfully complete the migration and pass tests, but Response B shows more thorough implementation of xUnit.v3 best practices and clearer verification of all required changes. Response A's main advantage is showing explicit package removal syntax, but Response B's overall approach is more rigorous and future-proof."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate basic xUnit.net v2 project to v3
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B is significantly better because it fully satisfies all rubric criteria, while Response A omits a critical requirement (IsTestingPlatformApplication=false). Additionally, Response B uses more recent package versions (4.0.1 and 4.0.0 vs 3.2.2 and 3.1.5), demonstrating better alignment with current xunit.v3 versions. Both achieved passing tests, but Response B's completeness and systematic approach using the migration skill makes it the superior migration."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate project with YTest.MTP.XUnit2 to xUnit.net v3 preserving MTP
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B fully satisfies all rubric criteria while Response A critically misses criterion 2 (UseMicrosoftTestingPlatformRunner=true). The rubric explicitly states that this property must be added "to preserve MTP," and Response A's omission of this configuration represents a significant deviation from the specified migration requirements. While both responses achieve working tests and complete the package upgrade, Response B's adherence to all stated rubric criteria makes it substantially better. Additionally, Response B uses a newer version of xunit.v3 (4.0.1 vs 3.2.2) and explicitly enabled the TestingPlatformRunner property through configuration rather than relying on implicit behavior.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate xUnit v2 packages managed via Central Package Management
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B meets all four rubric criteria, while Response A fails to set OutputType=Exe, which is an explicit requirement. Both responses successfully complete the core migration (renaming packages, updating references, tests pass), but Response B provides a more complete v3 migration by including the OutputType=Exe and IsTestingPlatformApplication=false properties, which are important for proper xUnit.net v3 Testing Platform integration. Additionally, Response B uses a more current xUnit.v3 version (4.0.1 vs 3.0.0). Both test suites pass successfully, preventing this from being a "much-better" verdict, but Response B's completeness against all rubric criteria makes it objectively superior."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recognize project already on xUnit.net v3 — no migration needed
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses correctly identify that the project already uses xUnit.net v3 and appropriately make no changes. However, Response B provides more thorough verification and documentation of the no-op status, including NuGet feed confirmation, complete dependency graph inspection, specific test discovery metrics, and platform verification. This more comprehensive analysis gives higher confidence in the assessment and provides better documentation for the user. While Response A is more concise and efficient, the superior quality and completeness of Response B's verification outweighs the resource difference in this context where confidence in a migration decision is important.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update BeforeAfterTestAttribute overrides with IXunitTest parameter
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B successfully completed a comprehensive xUnit v2-to-v3 migration that addressed all critical rubric requirements. It not only updated package references and project configuration (like Response A), but crucially also updated the DatabaseSetupAttribute class to match v3's changed BeforeAfterTestAttribute API by adding IXunitTest parameters to the Before and After method overrides and updating base method calls accordingly. Response A appears to have only addressed the project file changes without updating the test attribute class code, which is a critical omission for a proper v2-to-v3 migration. Response B's test verification (1 passed) confirms the migration was successful, while Response A's claim that tests pass unchanged is suspect given the API incompatibility it did not address."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update Xunit.Combinatorial and Xunit.StaFact companion packages
judgeRationales.rationale: While Response A selected newer package versions (winning on 3 of 4 individual criteria), it critically failed to implement the OutputType=Exe requirement, which is an explicit rubric criterion. Response B successfully completed all four migration requirements, verified successful build completion, and followed a more systematic approach. The failure to set OutputType=Exe in Response A is a significant compliance gap that outweighs the benefit of choosing newer package versions, especially since both sets of versions are functional—the real difference is that Response B met all specified requirements while Response A did not.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update custom FactAttribute to include source information parameters
judgeRationales.rationale: Response A completed a partial migration by updating package versions and running tests, but left a critical gap: the xUnit3003 compiler warning explicitly shows that custom attribute constructors were not updated with required caller source information parameters. This is a direct failure against all four rubric criteria. Response B, guided by a dedicated migration skill, completed a more thorough migration that includes updating both RetryFactAttribute and ConditionalTheoryAttribute with proper caller source information, as evidenced by the absence of xUnit3003 warnings and explicit claims in the output. Response B also added necessary properties (OutputType, IsTestingPlatformApplication) and resolved to more recent package versions. While both report passing tests, only Response B actually completed the migration correctly per xUnit.net v3 best practices."

Both responses executed flawlessly with zero errors and maintained the existing xUnit framework. judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detect MSTest v2 on VSTest and recommend migration path
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B is better aligned with the rubric criteria and provides clearer, more actionable guidance. It explicitly identifies the current platform (VSTest), recommends a sensible sequential upgrade path (v2→v3→v4) as the primary approach, and mentions the optional VSTest to MTP migration. Response A, while technically more detailed (fetching NuGet package info), misses key points: it doesn't explicitly state the current VSTest platform, it recommends a more aggressive .NET 10 LTS jump as the primary option rather than incremental MSTest upgrades, and it had one fetch error. Response B executed without errors and is more concise and actionable. The difference is 'slightly-better' rather than 'much-better' because both correctly identify MSTest v2.2.10, and Response A does provide additional version detail from NuGet feeds.

Response B failed to complete the task due to file access denial and made zero changes, meeting 0 of 4 criteria. The task specifically requires updating package references and making necessary configuration changes—only Response A accomplished this."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate project with YTest.MTP.XUnit2 to xUnit.net v3 preserving MTP
judgeRationales.rationale: Response A completed a functional migration from xUnit v2 to v3 with verified passing tests. It successfully removed the old packages, added the new xunit.v3 package, made the project executable, and enabled MTP support (with a slightly different property name that proved functional). Response B encountered editor authorization restrictions and made zero changes to the project, failing to deliver any part of the migration. While Response A's property name differs slightly from the rubric specification, the working test results demonstrate the migration is correct. Response B's complete inability to modify files makes it substantially worse.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate xUnit v2 packages managed via Central Package Management
judgeRationales.rationale: Response A successfully migrated the project from xUnit v2 to v3, completing 3 of 4 explicit criteria with all tests passing. Response B encountered tool limitations that prevented any file modifications, resulting in zero completed criteria and a completely failed migration. This is a substantial quality gap: Response A delivered a working migration while Response B delivered nothing."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recognize project already on xUnit.net v3 — no migration needed
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update BeforeAfterTestAttribute overrides with IXunitTest parameter
judgeRationales.rationale: Response A successfully completed the entire xUnit.net v2→v3 migration, meeting all four rubric criteria and achieving passing tests. Response B failed to complete any file modifications, with the editor blocking patch application due to filesystem path restrictions. Response A recovered from tool failures by using bash commands, demonstrating adaptability, while Response B was unable to work around its tool limitations. The difference is substantial: a fully working migration with all changes applied versus a completely blocked migration with zero file modifications."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update Xunit.Combinatorial and Xunit.StaFact companion packages
judgeRationales.rationale: Response A successfully completed the full xUnit.net v2 to v3 migration, meeting all four rubric criteria. The project now references xunit.v3 4.0.1, has all companion packages updated to compatible versions, OutputType is set to Exe, and the build succeeds. Response B completely failed to complete the migration—it encountered file access restrictions and made zero changes to the project, meeting none of the four criteria. While Response B correctly identified what needed to be done, it did not execute any of the required modifications, leaving the project in its original v2 state."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update custom FactAttribute to include source information parameters
judgeRationales.rationale: Response A successfully completed the entire xUnit.net v2→v3 migration: it updated packages to xunit.v3.mtp-off 4.0.1 and runner 4.0.0, applied caller-information parameters to both custom attributes via the xUnit3003 analyzer, made the project executable, preserved VSTest configuration, and verified tests pass. Response B correctly diagnosed the requirements but failed to execute any changes—its apply_patch tool rejected file modifications due to workspace constraints, leaving the project completely unmigrated and meeting none of the rubric criteria."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate basic xUnit v2 project to MSTest v4 preserving VSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Both produce a working, verified MSTest conversion under VSTest, but B better matches the explicit package-management requirement by using the MSTest metapackage and updating the stale test SDK reference. A's separate framework/adapter package approach is functional but misses that stated criterion.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate basic xUnit v3 project to MSTest v4 preserving VSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve AwesomeAssertions package and every import form
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve effective assembly and class owners on methods
judgeRationales.rationale: B satisfies the key explicit MSTest v4 requirement while preserving VSTest, net8.0, test discovery, and owner metadata. A's otherwise sound ownership conversion is undermined by migrating only to MSTest 3.6.4 rather than v4.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve type and sequence assertion semantics
judgeRationales.rationale: Both deliver a correct MSTest v4 conversion that preserves all required assertion semantics, leaves the TFM and VSTest runner intact, and verifies three passing tests. Their package-management approaches differ but are both supported by their successful verified runs.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve xUnit parallelization default with [assembly: Parallelize]
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recognize project already on MSTest
judgeRationales.rationale: Both reach the correct no-op conclusion and preserve the project, but B provides the required `dotnet test` verification and precise passing-test result. The substantive outcome is otherwise the same.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stop when target framework is unsupported by MSTest v4
judgeRationales.rationale: B delivers the correct compatible migration, preserves the target framework, validates the build, accurately explains why v4 cannot be used on net7.0, and gives actionable alternatives. A's basic conversion compiles, but it incorrectly presents an old MSTest v3 version as the latest and omits the key v4/net7 compatibility decision.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Consolidate xunit.extensibility packages and remove xunit.abstractions
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy every stated migration requirement. B is slightly stronger in reporting end-to-end dotnet test verification and explicitly distinguishes the expected zero-test result; its additional xunit.v3 reference is unnecessary for the shown helper-only project but does not undermine the requested changes.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert async void test methods to async Task
judgeRationales.rationale: The actual migration and verification are effectively identical and successful in both. B's final summary more explicitly addresses the v3 async-void incompatibility and configured-feed restore requirement.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert string-based attribute constructors to typeof syntax
judgeRationales.rationale: Both are successful, verified migrations that satisfy the attribute-focused task. B is slightly stronger as a final delivery because it gives more precise package/runner compatibility context, explains why VSTest was retained, documents resolved versions, and reports restore/build/test verification. A is clearer on the specific Type-versus-strings explanation, but that does not outweigh B's marginally more complete migration report.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detect incompatible target framework and stop migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Although A produced a technically verified migration after changing the target framework, the explicit evaluation workflow requires stopping at the incompatible net462 target and asking the user to upgrade first. B satisfies all of those stated requirements.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate Xunit.SkippableFact to xUnit.net v3 built-in skip APIs
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy every specified migration criterion and verify a working test run. B is slightly stronger overall because it additionally verifies the enabled feature branch as well as skip behavior, while retaining the existing VSTest configuration through an explicit compatible project setting. A's Microsoft.Testing.Platform switch is also valid and successfully tested.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate basic xUnit.net v2 project to v3
judgeRationales.rationale: Both produce a passing xUnit v3 migration, but B follows the project's existing VSTest configuration and includes the necessary IsTestingPlatformApplication=false setting. A's alternate MTP switch works in this environment but misses the expected configuration and alters global runner selection unnecessarily.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate project with YTest.MTP.XUnit2 to xUnit.net v3 preserving MTP
judgeRationales.rationale: B meets every stated migration requirement and verifies the result. A produces a passing project but omits the explicit UseMicrosoftTestingPlatformRunner=true configuration required to preserve the project's MTP setup. [Magnitude reduced to "slightly-better": the position-swapped pass judged this "slightly-better", so the more confident "much-better" was downgraded.]

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate xUnit v2 packages managed via Central Package Management
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recognize project already on xUnit.net v3 — no migration needed
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update BeforeAfterTestAttribute overrides with IXunitTest parameter
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update Xunit.Combinatorial and Xunit.StaFact companion packages
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy every explicit migration criterion and compile successfully. B is slightly stronger because it explicitly preserves the project's existing VSTest configuration with IsTestingPlatformApplication=false and accurately explains the configured-feed version choice. A makes an unnecessary global runner change and overstates its comparison to the original project: its logged original-v2 check actually failed at build time from a missing FrameworkReference rather than identically at runtime.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update custom FactAttribute to include source information parameters
judgeRationales.rationale: Both complete the required source-info migration and validate passing tests. B is slightly preferable because it preserves the existing VSTest global configuration and explicitly disables the Testing Platform application mode to retain a working VSTest-based project, rather than changing repository-level test-runner configuration; it also clearly records the compatibility rationale. A is nevertheless a valid, verified migration.

judgeRationales.rationale: B completes the requested xUnit v3 package and project-configuration migration and verifies all tests pass. A incorrectly concludes v3 is unavailable, deliberately leaves the project on v2, and therefore fails the core task despite a successful v2 build.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate project with YTest.MTP.XUnit2 to xUnit.net v3 preserving MTP
judgeRationales.rationale: B performs the actual v2-to-v3 package and runner migration required by the task and verifies it succeeds. A does not migrate to v3 at all, replaces the existing MTP setup with a v2 VSTest setup, and makes materially misleading claims about completion.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate xUnit v2 packages managed via Central Package Management
judgeRationales.rationale: B completed the requested migration, preserved central package management, and verified build plus successful execution and discovery. Its report has minor inconsistencies (it labels the target 3.1.0 while stating xunit.v3 1.0.0, and dotnet test showed no tests), but this is overwhelmingly better than A's false claim that xUnit v3 is unavailable and refusal to migrate.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recognize project already on xUnit.net v3 — no migration needed
judgeRationales.rationale: B correctly diagnosed the already-complete migration, made no unnecessary edits, and verified the tests passed. A reached a valid final configuration but performed and reported an unnecessary downgrade/re-upgrade, contrary to the task context and less trustworthy.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update BeforeAfterTestAttribute overrides with IXunitTest parameter
judgeRationales.rationale: B at least changes the project to xunit.v3 packages and verifies a passing build/test, whereas A explicitly falls back to xUnit 2.9.3 despite claiming completion. However, B seriously undermines the migration by deleting the existing database setup attribute rather than adapting its v3 method signatures, and both fail every specified source-level requirement.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update Xunit.Combinatorial and Xunit.StaFact companion packages
judgeRationales.rationale: B completes the requested xUnit v3 migration using the v3 packages, updates the related extensions, adds the required executable output type, and verifies passing tests. A fails the central task and reports an erroneous release blocker while leaving the project on xUnit v2.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Update custom FactAttribute to include source information parameters
judgeRationales.rationale: B completed the essential v3 custom-attribute API migration, built with zero warnings, and ran both tests successfully. A updated the package and ran tests, but missed the core caller-information changes explicitly needed for custom FactAttribute/TheoryAttribute subclasses and left analyzer warnings.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Decline request to write new tests
judgeRationales.rationale: Both produced validated xUnit test expansions aligned with the user's request. A is marginally stronger from the reported coverage because it includes associative behavior in addition to the shared arithmetic, boundary, overflow, commutativity, and repeatability coverage, and it completed validation without an initial failed command.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detect MSTest v2 on VSTest and recommend migration path
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly identifies the testing framework, its major-version migration path, and runner-platform migration options. A correctly finds net8.0 and package versions, but substantially misinterprets 'migrations' as EF/database or .NET target-framework migration and misses the requested MSTest/VSTest guidance.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detect xUnit v2 and route to xUnit v3 migration
judgeRationales.rationale: B is more grounded in the actual project and reports concrete package versions and changes made. However, it omits the old v2.9.3 version in its final answer, does not mention OutputType=Exe, and overstates API compatibility. A is reasonable general guidance but is less project-specific and its wildcard version examples are not a precise upgrade prescription.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Execute targeted MSTest v2 to v3 migration
judgeRationales.rationale: A completed the requested package upgrade, resolved the resulting compatibility/build issue, and demonstrated success with 3/3 passing tests. B made the basic version change but left compatibility unaddressed and provided no successful validation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Execute targeted xUnit v2 to v3 migration
judgeRationales.rationale: A completed the framework-only migration, preserved VSTest, resolved a package-version issue, and verified the final project by building and running all tests. B made a plausibly correct package edit but failed to validate the build, leaving the task's central success condition unproven.
